Grover C. Thomsen and R. H. Roark developed their red cream soda at their Waco bottling operation in 1937, and it was first sold under the name Waco Red Cream Soda — the label tying it directly to its hometown. The shortened name "Big Red" didn't come until 1959, when a San Austin-area bottler coined the phrase to describe the drink ("it's big, and it's red"), and the brand was officially renamed in the late 1960s under the company that became Big Red, Ltd.

A common source of confusion is that vintage Sun Tang-branded bottles circulate among collectors, since the Thomsen and Roark enterprise bottled other flavors under various labels; but the red cream soda itself went to market in 1937 as Waco Red Cream Soda.

The game was played in Corsicana — it was a home contest for the Oil Citys, which is why Justin "Nig" Clarke's record-setting eight home runs (in eight at-bats) came in front of the Corsicana faithful on 15 June 1902. Texarkana was simply the visiting club that day. The confusion on this point comes from sloppy scoreline convention: in historical box scores of that era, the home team was sometimes listed second, so "Corsicana 51, Texarkana 3" is sometimes transcribed or remembered as an away game. But the Texas League records and contemporary Corsicana newspaper accounts are clear that the contest took place on the Oil Citys' own diamond, where the short porches (the grounds were famously compact) helped produce the 51–3 blowout — still the highest run total by one team in organized baseball history.
